definitions.explanation: Death that occurs abruptly and unexpectedly, without prior warning or prolonged illness. Used in both medical and general contexts.

examples.japanese: {同僚|どうりょう}が{急死|きゅうし}して{皆|みな}{驚|おどろ}いた。
examples.english: Everyone was shocked when our colleague died suddenly.

examples.japanese: {心臓|しんぞう}{発作|ほっさ}による{急死|きゅうし}だった。
examples.english: It was a sudden death from a heart attack.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いスポーツ{選手|せんしゅ}の{急死|きゅうし}が{相次|あいつ}ぎ、{健康|けんこう}{管理|かんり}の{重要性|じゅうようせい}が{問|と}われている。
examples.english: A string of sudden deaths among young athletes has raised questions about the importance of health management.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in news reports and medical contexts. Often associated with heart-related conditions, overwork ({過労死|かろうし}), or hidden health problems. Can be used as a する verb: {急死|きゅうし}する (to die suddenly).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急死|きゅうし}する (to die suddenly)
- {突然|とつぜん}の{急死|きゅうし} (a sudden, unexpected death)
- {心臓|しんぞう}{急死|きゅうし} (cardiac sudden death)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {突然死|とつぜんし}: sudden death — very similar; slightly more emphasis on the unexpectedness
- {過労死|かろうし}: death from overwork — a specific cause of sudden death, well-known internationally
